input.quote: Such inspections may be made no more than once each Calendar Year, at reasonable times and on reasonable prior written notice.
input.rationale: Two audit rights bind Ono. Section 7.4 (p0481-p0482) is close to the playbook position — once each Calendar Year, independent accounting firm reasonably acceptable to Ono, confidentiality undertaking, Array bears cost — but the notice is only \"reasonable prior written notice\" rather than a fixed minimum, and the cost-shifting underpayment threshold is redacted ([ * ]) so it cannot be confirmed at 10 percent. Separately, Section 4.9(a) (p0359) gives Array (or its representative) an open-ended right to enter Ono facilities on \"reasonable advance notice\" with no frequency cap at all, which is walk-away territory (unlimited audits). We therefore target the fallback: fixed 15 days' notice, once per year, and Array bearing cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent. Business hours, independent auditor and auditor confidentiality (preferred elements) are already present in the existing bargain and were left untouched.

mappings.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.

proposal.summary: Fix audit notice period and underpayment threshold in Section 7.4 and add frequency/notice limits to the open-ended Section 4.9 inspection right.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We fixed the audit notice at fifteen (15) days and set the cost-shifting underpayment threshold at ten percent (10%) in Section 7.4, and capped the Section 4.9 inspection right at once per year on the same notice, since as drafted it is unlimited and unquantified.
